title: Ephemeral telemetry digger and safe-mode restart helper
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: On high-severity incidents teams frequently need a bounded, time-boxed snapshot of logs/metrics/traces plus a minimal, vetted remediation path that can be executed by on-call without escalating to infra. This PR introduces two cooperating features: (1) an ephemeral telemetry collector (telemetry-digger) that attaches to a trace/span id and harvests relevant logs, short-term metrics, and a CPU/heap flame snapshot from the last 2 minutes; and (2) a safe-mode restart helper that generates a minimal restart plan (graceful restart, circuit-breaker toggle, or node drain + scale-up) and provides a one-click, audited action via incident-bot.

Design & motivation: The goal is to reduce time-to-evidence and reduce noisy restarts. The telemetry-digger collects bounded artifacts (configurable TTL, default 30m) and stores them with a short lifecycle in the incident-bot ephemeral bucket. The safe-mode restart helper uses a rule engine (configurable policies per service) to prefer low-risk actions first and emits a JSON plan that ops can review before execution. This avoids full runbook handoffs for common transient failure modes.

What this PR changes (summary): - New command: /dig-telemetry <trace_id> which returns a signed artifact URL and short diagnostic summary. - New command: /safe-restart <service> [--quick|--dry-run] which returns a recommended plan and, when confirmed, executes an audited restart with rollback hooks. - Added an artifacts handler and short-lifecycle storage + retention enforcement. - Small policy engine for restart heuristics with unit-tested rule sets. - End-to-end tests that simulate a transient OOM and an API spike to exercise both commands.

Checklist: - [x] UX: slash command handlers and consistent CLI output - [x] Security: signed URLs + scoped role for ephemeral bucket - [x] Tests: unit and e2e smoke tests added - [x] Docs: brief runbook snippets and usage examples in commands README - [x] Ops: added Prometheus metrics (dig_requests_total, safe_restart_executions_total)

Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: Add telemetry-digger service, collection pipeline, retention enforcement - 2b3c4d5: Implement /dig-telemetry slash command + artifact signing - 3c4d5e6: Add safe-mode policy engine and restart executor - 4d5e6f7: Integrate restart confirmation flow and audit events - 5e6f7g8: Add e2e tests and ci job for flakiness guard

Changed files (high-level): - cmd/incident-bot/commands/telemetry_digger.go - cmd/incident-bot/commands/safe_restart.go - internal/collector/digger_service.go - internal/policies/safe_restart_engine.go - internal/artifacts/ephemeral_store.go - tests/e2e/test_digger_safe_restart.sh - docs/commands/telemetry_and_restart.md

Review notes & discussion: - Diego: "Can we avoid writing raw logs into the ephemeral bucket? prefer gzipped, redacted blobs." -> Implemented redaction + gzip in artifacts handler.
- Hannah: "Add a rate-limit per-project on /dig-telemetry" -> Added token-bucket limiter and a per-team quota metric; documented behavior.
- Marcus: "How do we ensure restart won't destabilize an already degraded cluster?" -> Policy engine now queries recent 5m error rate/replica health and will only allow 'aggressive' restarts when cluster health > 90%; otherwise it recommends canary drain + warm replacement.
- Author (Asha): Follow-ups: added configuration knobs in config.yaml.example, included CI unit tests for policy decisions, and left a TODO to expose policy variables in the Console UI (tracked in ENG-3245).

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - linters: pass (fixed a couple of vet warnings) - e2e: initial run had one flaky test (test_digger_timeout) -> rerun succeeded - security-scan: pass - deployment-preview: generated and evaluated

Merge: Squash-and-merge after approvals. Merge commit message includes summary and linked Linear items. Post-merge actions: - run migration to add ephemeral bucket lifecycle - create alert rule for unexpected artifact TTL growth - add a small KB item to on-call docs

Usage examples (short): - /dig-telemetry 7a1f3e2c -> Returns: "Telemetry artifact: https://ephem.example.net/art/abcd1234 (expires in 30m)" and a short structured summary with top-5 error messages and a flame snapshot link. - /safe-restart api-service --dry-run -> Returns recommended plan; confirm by clicking the approve button in the chat and incident-bot executes the plan and records the audit event.

Rollback & mitigation: The restart executor runs pre-checks and creates a 'rollback ticket' in the incident if anything fails; the executor also supports an automatic rollback window (configurable, default 5m). The artifact store auto-deletes after TTL.

Why this is different: Many prior PRs focused on playbook generation and snapshotting; this PR pairs a lightweight, bounded telemetry collector with a tightly-scoped remediation executor designed for low-friction on-call actions while preserving auditability and safety.
